long_biography.plain_text:
Classic boats were woven into Earl McMillen III's upbringing in Georgia. His family cruised a 1920s wooden vessel and spent time at Lake Rabun, where he watched craftsmen revive vintage runabouts. After his younger brother died, McMillen and his father undertook a two-year restoration that carried him north to Newport and turned an absorbing project into a vocation.

A Columbia history graduate, McMillen created a specialist enterprise to acquire, restore and maintain significant American vessels. He later developed a fractional model in which groups of partners fund projects and share access while his team manages craftsmen, crews and cruising. The structure assembled one of the country's notable collections of operational classic craft. It also made it possible to rescue larger vessels whose preservation demanded sustained capital, technical knowledge and long-term stewardship.
